name: Old Lilac
lede: Old Lilac is a dulled, greyed lilac first recorded in Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary, dated to 1926.

sections.title: Lilac, muted
sections.body:
The library records Old Lilac from Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary, plate 45 H 6, first recorded in 1926 [1]. Our computed classification gives it a moderate purple, darker and less saturated than the flower word [[lilac]] it is built from [1]. As with [[old-lavender|Old Lavender]], "old" here marks a dulled, worn-looking cast rather than any real age [1].

The nearest named color in the library is Dull Dark Purple, about 3.3 units away by CIEDE2000, close to [[plum]] but darker than either [[dahlia-purple|Dahlia Purple]] or [[purplish-red|Purplish Red]] [1]. In LCH terms it measures lightness 40, chroma 29, hue 328 degrees, Munsell 8.5P 3.9/6.2 [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this color in only 3 of 23,781 paintings, well under one tenth of one percent, as photographed [2]. All three are from the 1800s and 1900s; none appears before then [2]. France and the United States each account for one of the three, and no single painter here carries it more than once [2]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, so a color match is not a pigment test [2].
